rationale: enc-rc4 is a tiny, hot-loop stream-cipher kernel (KSA/PRGA dominate execution), so the profile's lack of source metadata implies a small number of dense, frequently-executed functions where control-flow transforms pay heavy runtime penalties. Cheap, semantics-preserving arithmetic and structural passes are favored: SUB gets high weights across all dimensions since instruction substitution adds strong static-analysis resistance with negligible overhead in ALU-heavy cipher code, and SPLIT is similarly low-risk for breaking up basic blocks. IBR and ICALL are kept at moderate weights — indirect branching and indirect calls obscure the call/branch graph well but add real dispatch overhead in the tight PRGA loop, so their RuntimeCost weights are trimmed so they are preferentially applied to colder functions. IGV provides good diversity cheaply on a small program. BCF and FLA are heavily down-weighted (especially RuntimeCost/SizeCost) because bogus-edge insertion and control-flow flattening would inflate the hot-loop branch misprediction and dispatch costs and bloat a function set that is already tiny; they remain enabled at low weight so the feature-driven selector can still apply them to any cold helper functions where their strong security payoff comes at acceptable cost, preserving correctness across the board since all passes are semantics-preserving.
